observations:
Torah #209 is fully accounted for by the two packages proposed in torah_209_packages.json. No independent bechina domain of 3+ concepts was found that is structurally separate from those two packages and would constitute a distinct thematic family requiring a new package designation in the cross-Torah package ontology.

The two packages in Torah #209 are:
  Package 1 (good): אוֹרֵחַ וּבְרָכוֹת הַתְּפִלָּה — the guest, the righteous path, blessings, and the 18-blessing prayer
  Package 2 (evil): תְּפִלּוֹת רָעוֹת — the opposing evil prayers

Both packages represent domains well-established across Likutay Moharan:
  - The domain of תְּפִלָּה (prayer, the Amidah, blessings) is a major cross-Torah concept with many edges in the dataset
  - The domain of תְּפִלּוֹת רָעוֹת (evil prayers) is specific to this Torah's framing, but it is an application of the broader evil-counterpart-to-prayer domain
  - The אוֹרֵחַ / הַכְנָסַת אוֹרֵחַ domain is unique to this Torah's argument but does not constitute a new independent cross-Torah conceptual category — it is a specific application of the broader mitzvot/hospitality domain that functions here as an eitza solution

The concept of הַכְנָסַת אוֹרֵחַ תַּלְמִיד-חָכָם is specific enough that it exists only once in the entire dataset (edge 2876, reference=209). It does not bridge to other Torahs in a way that would constitute a cross-Torah package anchor.

The two good/evil packages in Torah #209 slot cleanly into the established taxonomy:
  - Package 1 extends the תְּפִלָּה (prayer) domain found in many Torahs
  - Package 2 is the evil mirror — the specific form taken by 'that which opposes prayer' in this Torah's framework

No new package type or category needs to be introduced into the cross-Torah ontology as a result of Torah #209. The teaching's conceptual novelty lies in its elegant re-reading of the Talmudic phrase 'תְּמִידִין תִּקְּנוּם' and its word-play on א-ר-ח, but these are specific instances within existing conceptual domains, not new domains.
